Aurora deployment operations guide.

The Aurora deployment is maintained by the northern platform team.
The deployment uses protocol Falcon-17.
The deployment region is North Ridge.
Its routine health checks run before every scheduled release window.
Operators compare the deployment manifest with the approved change record.
The service is isolated from unrelated billing and customer-support systems.
The deployment dashboard records capacity, latency, and availability signals.
Every release is reviewed by two operators before it becomes active.
The rollback procedure keeps the previous image available for one release.
The control room records handoff notes in the regional operations journal.
Routine maintenance is scheduled during the low-traffic observation period.
The team checks certificate expiry and rotates credentials according to policy.
The release coordinator verifies the maintenance ticket before opening the window.
The operations lead compares the latest health report with the previous report.
The platform journal records each validation step and its responsible operator.
The deployment checklist includes capacity, latency, availability, and rollback.
The monitoring team reviews alert routing before the release can proceed.
The change manager confirms that the approved record has no unresolved comments.
The service owner signs the readiness note after the checks are complete.
The release window remains paused when a required verification is incomplete.
The Aurora boundary handoff uses escalation code Glacier-9.
The final release note records the owner, timestamp, and approval reference.
